# Pinned Chorala widget

This is the MIT-licensed **widget package**, not Chorala's AGPL server.
The observed widget manifest declares Preact 10.29.2; both MIT notices are
retained in this directory and embedded in the served generated asset.
See `NOTICE` for source URLs, retrieval date and the pinned distribution hash.
The exact Git revision producing the distributed bundle is unknown.

`upstream-widget.js` is the unchanged public distribution. Do not edit it.
`widget.js` is generated by `scripts/build-chorala-widget.mjs` and committed
so source imports and tests work before a production build. Vite imports it
with `?url`, producing a content-hashed same-origin script asset.

```sh
npm run build:chorala-widget
node scripts/build-chorala-widget.mjs --check
```

The generator runs before `npm run build`, uses no network or new dependencies,
and rejects a different source hash or non-unique patch anchors. Upstream updates
require reviewing the new source, licenses, hash and patches together; no build
silently downloads a new widget.

The local patch adds an API-client `setJwt` operation, a `refreshIdentity` command
and a `supportsIdentityRefresh` capability flag. Refresh mutates the existing
client's header state, preserving the mounted UI, draft and attachments. Ordinary
`identify` remains destructive and is used only at account boundaries. Clearing a
JWT with `refreshIdentity({})` removes its header without retaining an expired
identity after SSO has explicitly been disabled.

The widget still calls the configured Chorala API directly. Exact application
origins must be allowed in Chorala; self-hosting this script does not remove CORS
requirements. Satflux CSRF headers are never sent to Chorala. The proxy endpoint
is not exempted from CSRF.
